Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. A common Judgment was passed on 31.01.2019 in MVC No.23/2016 and MVC No.25/2016 by the Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Yadgir (for short 'the Tribunal').
This appeal is filed against the judgment and award in MVC No.25 of 2016.

3. The claimant met with an accident on 10.02.2015 due to the rash and negligent driving of the NC:
2025:KHC-K:6631 HC-KAR driver of the Innova Car bearing registration No.AP-21/ AN-1221 and sustained grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.17,00,000/-.

4. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.6,34,000/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.

5. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken his income only at Rs.6,000/- per month and granted lesser compensation; as his right leg was amputed above the knee, PW.3 assessed the disability at 85%, but the Tribunal has erred in taking the disability at only 50% to the whole body.

Therefore, requested for enhancement of Bannappa vs C Shravan Kumar And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79238506/

sentences.text: NC: 2025:KHC-K:6631 HC-KAR 6.
Heard the arguments of both sides.
7. Though the appellant stated that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, he has not produced any income proof.
Therefore, as the accident is of the year 2015, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.8,000/- per month.
As it is a case of amputation, the doctor has assessed the disability at 85% under Ex.P11.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability at 85% as per the evidence of the doctor.
As he was aged 60 years as per the wound certificate, the multiplier was rightly taken as '9'.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.8,000 x 12 x 9 x 85% = Rs.7,34,400/-.
8.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,55,967/- towards medical expenses and it needs not interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6631 HC-KAR 9.
The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 84 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.50,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.40,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
10. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of six months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.48,000/-
(Rs.8,000 x 6) for loss of income during laid up period.
11. PW.2 suggested the estimated cost of the artificial limb at Rs.1,25,000/- and the said amount is granted towards future medical expenses.

12. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6631 HC-KAR Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.1,55,967/-
Future medical expenses Rs.1,25,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.7,34,400/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.48,000/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.40,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
Total Rs.12,53,367/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.6,34,000/-
Bannappa vs C Shravan Kumar And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79238506/
3 Enhancement Rs.6,19,367/-
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,19,367/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

13. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.6,19,367/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
However, as per order dated 24.07.2023, the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6631 HC-KAR appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 662 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
